expectations.text: GOVERN function added (elevating governance/supply-chain risk strategy), reorganizing former ID categories
expectations.evidence: A sixth function: Govern (GV)... CSF 1.1 embedded governance activities across the Identify and Protect functions (mainly ID.GV and ID.RM). CSF 2.0 pulls governance out; ID.SC moved into GV.SC and expanded

expectations.text: Scope broadened: from critical infrastructure to all organizations
expectations.evidence: CSF 1.1 was written with a critical-infrastructure lens; CSF 2.0 explicitly targets organizations of all sizes and sectors

expectations.text: Structural changes: categories/subcategories reorganized and renumbered — requires subcategory-level remapping, not a rename
expectations.evidence: Subcategory-level remap shown: 108 in CSF 1.1 down to 106 in 2.0; mapping table (ID.GV-01 -> GV.PO-01 etc.); 'Validate specific subcategory mappings'

expectations.text: Mentions new support resources: implementation examples, quick-start guides, reference tool, community profiles
expectations.evidence: New resources named: 'searchable NIST CSF 2.0 Reference Tool, updated via the OLIR program' and 'added Quick Start Guides for SMBs, enterprise risk managers, and government'

expectations.text: Gives a sane migration path: map existing 1.1 profile to 2.0 subcategories, stand up GOVERN outcomes, refresh target profile and roadmap
expectations.evidence: Migration checklist maps 1.1 practices to new GV homes ('map your existing ID.GV/ID.RM practices to their new GV homes'), stands up GOVERN first, then supply chain and additive changes into the improvement cycle
